function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

I’m happy to help you pull the data you need, but I’ll need a bit more detail to call the telemetry function correctly.

The `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get` function requires four pieces of information:

| Parameter | What it represents | Example values |
|-----------|--------------------|----------------|
| `fabricName` | Name of the fabric you’re querying | `"test-de"` |
| `nodeId` | Numeric ID of the node you want data for | `12345` |
| `podId` | Numeric ID of the pod the node belongs to | `1` |
| `interfaceType` | Type of interface you’re interested in | `"svi"`, `"ethernet"`, `"loopback"`, or `"port-channel"` |
| `infoType` | Kind of information you want about that interface | `"interfaces"`, `"status"`, `"statistics"`, or `"errors"` |

Since you mentioned the IP address **23.31.32.1**, I assume you want to look up the node that has that IP. Unfortunately, the function doesn’t accept an IP address directly; it needs the numeric `nodeId`. If you already know the node’s ID (or can map the IP to a node ID), just plug it in.

**Example call (replace the placeholders with your actual values):**

```python
response = functions.telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get({
    "fabricName": "test-de",
    "nodeId": 12345,          # <-- replace with the node’s numeric ID
    "podId": 1,               # <-- replace with the pod’s numeric ID
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",   # <-- choose the interface type you need
    "infoType": "status"      # <-- choose the info type you need
})
print(response)
```

If you don’t yet know the node ID for the IP 23.31.32.1, you’ll need to look that up first (perhaps via your inventory system or a separate API that maps IPs to node IDs). Once you have the node ID, you can use the snippet above to fetch the desired interface information.

Let me know if you’d like help mapping the IP to a node ID, or if you have the node ID ready so we can proceed!
